history.heading: Salt and settlers
paragraphs: The Turks and Caicos Islands, a group of about 40 low-lying islands southeast of the Bahamas, were inhabited by the Taíno and Lucayan peoples, who were wiped out after European contact. Bermudian salt rakers settled Grand Turk in the late 17th century to harvest sea salt, which remained the main industry for centuries.

After the American Revolution, Loyalists established cotton plantations with enslaved Africans, which soon failed. The islands were governed from the Bahamas and later Jamaica, and became a separate British colony in 1962. In 1962 astronaut John Glenn splashed down nearby after the first US orbital flight.

history.heading: Modern era
paragraphs: In 2009 Britain suspended self-government for three years after an inquiry found widespread corruption. Hurricanes Irma and Maria hit the islands in 2017.

culture.heading: Island culture
paragraphs: English is official, and most residents are of African descent, along with many expatriates and Haitian migrants. Christianity is central. Ripsaw music, using a saw as an instrument, is local folk music. Conch is the national dish, celebrated at an annual conch festival.

politics.heading: British Overseas Territory
paragraphs: The Turks and Caicos Islands are a British Overseas Territory with an elected House of Assembly and a premier; a governor appointed by the British monarch handles defence, foreign affairs and security. Irregular migration from Haiti is a major issue.

economy.heading: Tourism and finance
paragraphs: Luxury tourism, centred on Grace Bay Beach on Providenciales, is the main industry, followed by offshore financial services and real estate. There is no income tax. The currency is the US dollar.
